title: ScenarioPack
description: contracts/demo/scenarios.v1.json (the main pack) and contracts/demo/faults.v1.json (the faults pack, D119): the single source of demo, e2e and fault traffic (SPEC §7.6, §2.13). Go cmd/trafficgen sends each request with X-TrustAgent-Scenario (test mode); the mock decision backend answers from mock_answers (fallback.mock_answers for the re-gated fallback answer), mock-upstream serves response (and fallback.response) as the upstream answer, and the mock judge answers from judge. --expect asserts expect against the response (headers, trailers, the SSE decision comment and the delivered text) and the stored trace.

scenarios.description: The scenarios in send order. The main pack is never empty; the faults pack starts empty and GO fills it (validate.mjs).

items.title: Scenario

sets.description: Selection tags for trafficgen --scenarios: s0 (the walking skeleton), demo, e2e, generated (answer_source generated), untagged (documents in shapes evidence extraction does not read, so the gate is not_assessed), knowledge (needs the knowledge add-on), faults (vendor-fault scenarios: only in contracts/demo/faults.v1.json, where every scenario carries it, D119). A phase tag (p3, p4, p5) marks a scenario that needs that gateway phase (streaming gating, block and fallback bodies, /v1/messages, /v1/completions, routes in config/policies.pending.yaml); trafficgen skips it unless --phase reaches that phase.

answer_source.description: scripted: the upstream answer is response (test_response). generated: the answer is produced by the real upstream when recording (record-demo); response is then only the mock-mode stand-in.

request.description: The request body sent by trafficgen (minus test_response). Unknown fields pass through to the upstream.

items.description: An OpenAI-style message. content may be a string or content parts (to exercise tolerant parsing, B3). Other fields (tool_call_id, tool_calls, name) pass through to the upstream request.

response.description: Scripted assistant text returned by the upstream in test mode.

mock_answers.description: Answers the mock decision backend returns for this scenario, keyed by question id: "<id>__v<version>" of each evaluator attached to the route that compile() sends (SPEC §2.9 step 5). Evaluators that compile excludes (for example no_evidence) are not asked and have no answer; evaluators that need no evidence are always asked (validate.mjs checks both against config/policies.yaml).

mock_faults.description: Vendor faults mock-upstream injects for this scenario (D119; faults pack only): decision for the decision-model endpoints, upstream for the LLM upstream. A value is a mock-upstream fault name (cmd/mock-upstream Faults), optionally counted: <name>@<n> faults the first n calls of one request (attempt and hedge share the count through X-Mock-Key) and answers normally after. trafficgen sends the scenario id as X-TrustAgent-Scenario; in test mode the gateway forwards it to a local decision backend (internal/jev/testheaders.go), and mock-upstream answers the decision requests that name it with decision (counted per X-Mock-Key, the trace id) and the LLM request of its conversation with upstream (counted per scenario until _mock/reset). A test-mode client may instead send X-TrustAgent-Scenario fault:<spec> directly: a forward-only value, never stored.

knowledge.description: Knowledge-base documents the scenario relies on (knowledge add-on, SPEC §7.1): the knowledge profile must hold them, and RetrieveContext returns them for this request, in order. Only on a route whose evidence.sources include knowledge.

fallback.description: The fallback answer of a scenario whose gate replaces the answer (route mode fallback, SPEC §2.12 Fallback). In test mode the gateway answers the fallback call with response (the scripted counterpart of test_response); mock-upstream serves it to a fallback request (its prompt carries the CONTEXT block); the mock decision backend answers the re-gate (attempt 1) with mock_answers when the state's assistant_response is response. The deep audit still audits the original answer.

mock_answers.description: Raw answers to the re-gate of the fallback answer, keyed like mock_answers.

expect.description: The re-gate decision (attempt 1). would_action pass or flag delivers the fallback; block applies fallback.on_fail.

anyOf.description: Mock judge fixture (LLM_PROVIDER=mock, AuditOptions.mock_scenario). claims[] in response order is the decomposer output ({claim, quote}); each entry's verdict, confidence, evidence and reasoning are the verifier output for that claim (verdict is the verifier's status), which the deep audit reports unchanged.

quote.description: Decomposer quote: a verbatim substring of response (validate.mjs checks it); the claim span is located from it.

evidence.description: Verifier evidence quotes, each verbatim from the request's evidence or the scenario's knowledge documents (validate.mjs checks they occur there).

anyOf.description: No LLM call is expected: the deep audit is not run or is NOT_ASSESSED at preflight. A mock judge call for this scenario is a fixture miss.

expect.description: The expected outcome, derived by hand from SPEC §2.9 under the policy the gateway loads (config/policies.yaml, plus config/policies.pending.yaml for phase-tagged scenarios), and cross-checked against the Go reference decide() by cmd/trafficgen tests. trafficgen --expect asserts the decision fields against what the response carries (headers; for streams also the trailers and the SSE decision comment; for observe routes, whose headers say deferred, the stored trace), the delivered text, and the settled trace. reasons must all be present (subset match).

mode.description: X-TrustAgent-Mode: the effective mode (the route mode, or flag when block or fallback meets a passthrough stream).

would_action.description: The decision's would_action. X-TrustAgent-Would-Action is sent only when it differs from action, so an absent header means would_action equals action.

max_risk.description: The decision's max_risk. X-TrustAgent-Risk carries it with 2 decimals and is absent when null.

reasons.description: X-TrustAgent-Reasons entries (comma-separated in the header, absent when empty).

checked_against.description: X-TrustAgent-Checked-Against value: evidence items per source, or none.

deep_audit.description: The decision's deep_audit class (SPEC §2.9); not a header.

audit_verdict.description: The deep-audit verdict the trace ends with. null when the answer is not audited (sampled_out, dropped, disabled). NOT_ASSESSED when there was nothing to check it against (X-TrustAgent-Audit: not_assessed, whether Go skipped the audit or the engine preflight answered), with no LLM call, so validate.mjs requires judge: null.

outcome.description: The single outcome the dashboard shows once the gate has decided (contracts/ui/outcomes.v1.json); validate.mjs derives it from status, action and would_action.

delivered_text.description: The assistant text the client receives (choice 0, the Anthropic text blocks, or the concatenated stream deltas) when it is not response: the route's block message for action block (style message), fallback.response for action fallback.

http_status.description: The HTTP status of the gateway response (a block with style error answers block.status).

degraded.description: Whether the decision is degraded (D119): a vendor fault left the gate without a full answer (status error:<kind>, timeout or partial), and the trace says the check did not complete. Absent: not asserted.

decision_model.description: What the decision-model client did for this request (D119), read from the stored trace: attempts counts vendor requests (retries and the hedge included), hedged whether a hedge was sent, late whether an answer arrived after the deadline and was recorded late. Absent fields are not asserted.

stream_decision.description: How a streamed response carries the decision (SPEC §2.12): comment is whether the stream holds the `: trustagent {...}` comment before its terminal event (stream_annotations: comment); trailers lists the X-TrustAgent-* headers that must arrive as HTTP trailers (Mode and Action on passthrough streams).

items.$comment: A scripted scenario needs response; fallback needs a fallback-mode route, knowledge a route with the knowledge source; mock_faults appears only in the faults pack, whose scenarios all carry the faults set and an explicit judge, fixtures or null (checked by validate.mjs).
